question: Why did the iData backup benchmark report about 1.1k task/s when the established dummy ceiling was about 12k task/s?
method: Current binaries, one local host, independent tasks, one variable changed at a time. Logical throughput includes frontend append time; service throughput is also recorded where available.
diagnosis: There is no order-of-magnitude scheduler or Controller regression: the current binary reproduces the about-12k dummy result at the matching 16-worker topology, even with one live empty iData per builtin task.
The about-1.1k result measures a different workload: one 16-slot Worker repeatedly fork/execs /bin/true and publishes one output per task.

Worker count is a performance dimension even at fixed total cores because each Worker has one control/execution event loop. Sixteen 1-core Workers sustain 12.17k builtin live-iData tasks/s; one 16-core Worker sustains only about 2.22k.

For command tasks, host process creation and Worker execution dominate: changing from one 16-core Worker to sixteen 1-core Workers raises live-iData throughput only from about 1.18k to 3.52k, far below builtin throughput.

Background backup is not the cause of the 12k-to-1.1k gap. In the paired 1x16 command runs its median logical cost is about 1.8 percent, within run noise; at 16x1 it runs asynchronously and drains after logical completion.
scope_limit: Single-host local diagnosis. These results compare software paths and Worker topology; they are not a multi-node network or storage-capacity claim.
